required_behavior: Repair only owned-process lifecycle in bounded_run and the minimum public probe plumbing needed to exercise it. Retain original response fixtures, arity matrix, record collection, receipt behavior and diagnostic policy for their separately assigned cards; do not claim those findings resolved.

Initialize cleanup state before spawning. From the instant Popen succeeds, every selector construction, pipe setup, registration, collection, and finalization operation must belong to an auditable cleanup policy. Selector creation must no longer sit outside that policy. A spawn failure must not signal a nonexistent child.

Create each invocation in its own session, keep the actual child ownership, and never signal a process group after its leader might have been reaped. waitpid(WNOHANG) returning the PID reaps it. Remove the incorrect ownership comment. Cover interruption during the ownership transition: setting a boolean only after waitpid returns is insufficient. Enter a no-signal region before a potentially reaping operation, or use another explicitly justified platform-supported mechanism that closes that interruption gap. Restore signal eligibility only upon a definite non-reaping observation. Unknown state is failure, not permission to signal.

Prepare fallible output/result material before reaping where practical. Status conversion, output construction, receipt writes, closing operations and deliberate post-reap faults must never flow back into a signal-capable exception handler. Do not install a generic handler that uses the original PID after ownership is released.

On setup failure, timeout, stream overflow, or an exception while ownership is established, signal only the owned group, boundedly drain both stdout and stderr without retaining beyond the existing caps, close stdin and all other pipe/selector resources, and boundedly reap. Cleanup has a fixed deadline, including drain and reap; do not use an unbounded wait or communicate. Preserve original failure reason alongside cleanup outcome. Failed or uncertain cleanup is a terminal failure and stops the suite.

Maintain concise lifecycle state for a public invocation: spawned PID, whether group signaling was attempted and the ownership phase of each attempt, leader-reap outcome, pipe closure outcome, cleanup status, and failure reason. Bound this to a fixed small set of transitions; it is not a general tracing system. For single lifecycle probes, persist this small object as lifecycle.json under the validated output directory even on failure when persistence is possible. Full matrix result.json remains the separate receipt card.

Preserve --adapter ABS and --output-dir ABS. Add only optional --scenario with a closed enum: matrix (default), lifecycle-normal, lifecycle-setup-failure, lifecycle-post-reap-exception, lifecycle-post-reap-interrupt, lifecycle-timeout, lifecycle-stdout-overflow, lifecycle-stderr-overflow. Reject unknown values before spawning. Each non-matrix scenario runs at most one real adapter invocation. No arbitrary command, Python expression, shell fragment, timeout, path-to-runner, dynamic plugin, or user-supplied fake program control.

The normal probe uses the existing success response. Setup failure raises a fixed deliberate exception after successful spawn and before selector setup. Post-reap exception and interruption probes deliberately raise a fixed ordinary exception or KeyboardInterrupt at the first designated post-reap finalization point. These are narrowly located public test controls, not monkeypatches or helper-call tests. Timeout and overflow probes change only the generated fake's fixed response behavior: finite sleep past the existing invocation deadline, or exactly 4097 literal bytes on the selected stream. The fake still cannot fork or use network.

The injected failure probes must exit nonzero and must not masquerade as matrix success. Their lifecycle object identifies the requested probe, observed failure, cleanup outcome, and signal attempts. A normal probe exits zero only after exact existing response validation and successful lifecycle completion. Do not claim a fixture's literal cleanup response is evidence of actual process cleanup.

Preserve fixed environment PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, private HOME, LANG=C; actual source adapter and sibling; absolute validated interpreter shebang; real /usr/bin/sandbox-exec and the original no-network/no-fork/write-only-output profile. No adapter copies or sandbox substitutes. Keep current 4096-byte stream caps, 16384-byte record cap, 10-second invocation and 180-second suite limits. Deadline-race repair is intentionally separate at launch27.
